ut.title: UT Inspection & Ultrasonic Thickness Testing | Beaumont, TX
ut.description: Ultrasonic thickness testing and weld UT for Beaumont and Golden Triangle refineries, petrochemical units, docks and tanks. Request an on-site quote.
ut.h1: Ultrasonic Testing and UT Thickness Inspection in Beaumont, Texas
ut.html:
Ultrasonic testing in Beaumont mostly means two things: wall-thickness surveys on aging refinery and petrochemical equipment, and shear-wave examination of repair and construction welds. Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to your Beaumont site for the agreed scope, with procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III. Send line lists, vessel tags or weld drawings through a Beaumont UT quote request and we will scope the survey around your outage or run schedule.

Where ultrasonic testing is used in Beaumont

Beaumont sits in the Golden Triangle with Port Arthur and Orange, the Texas stretch of the Sabine-Neches waterway whose refining history goes back to the Spindletop discovery of 1901. Energy and mining are the metro area's second-largest employment cluster, and chemicals and plastics are about three and a half times as concentrated here as in the nation overall. The ExxonMobil refinery in Beaumont started up a 250,000 barrel-a-day expansion in 2023 and now has 630,000 barrels a day of capacity, while the Port Arthur refineries run more than 720,000 barrels a day in one case, which means a very large inventory of heaters, columns, exchangers and miles of piping that need thickness monitoring.

The ports of Beaumont and Port Arthur rank among the top 25 US water ports by tonnage, mostly crude oil and refined products, so marine loading arms, dock piping, tank farm manifolds and storage tanks feed more ultrasonic work. New process capacity, including ethane crackers in Port Arthur, adds construction welds that are examined as units start up. Between those sites are pipe yards, fabrication shops and maintenance contractors that need weld examination before parts go into the field.

What UT finds around the Golden Triangle, and what it misses

Thickness surveys find general wall loss, localized pitting, erosion at fittings and thinning at injection and mixing points. These mechanisms are common in crude and heavy-feed units, in sour water and amine circuits and in water-cooled piping near the Neches and Sabine. A survey cannot say why the metal thinned; it says how much remains, and the owner's corrosion engineers interpret the cause. Weld examination finds planar flaws such as lack of fusion and cracks that radiography can miss when the flaw plane is tilted.

Limits matter. Rough, scaled or pitted outside surfaces scatter the signal, internal deposits can give false back-wall echoes, and a sparse grid can miss a small pit that lies between readings. Coarse-grained material, such as cast stainless and some weld metal, attenuates shear waves so heavily that a qualification block must show the technique works before the procedure is approved. Thin sections need an instrument and probe that can resolve the near-surface echo, which is why dual-element probes are standard on corroded lines.

Codes and acceptance criteria for Beaumont work

New and repaired pressure equipment is examined under ASME Section VIII Division 1, where Appendix 12 covers ultrasonic examination of welds, or under ASME B31.3 for process piping, whose paragraph 344.6 and Table 341.3.2 define the examination and acceptance. ASME Section V Article 4 sets the weld technique, Article 5 the material examination, and Article 23 carries SE-797 for contact thickness measurement. Structural weldments follow AWS D1.1 and pipeline girth welds follow API 1104.

In-service equipment falls under the owner's programs for API 510 vessels, API 570 piping and API 653 tanks, plus OSHA process safety management, 29 CFR 1910.119(j), which treats inspection and testing as part of mechanical integrity. The owner's authorized inspector makes the fitness and interval decisions; Atlantis supplies the readings and weld data. Texas boilers are regulated under Chapter 755 of the Health and Safety Code through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, and intrastate pipelines through the Railroad Commission of Texas.

Technique for thickness and weld examination

For a thickness survey, the technician locates the marked condition monitoring locations, prepares each point, and calibrates a dual-element probe on a step block of matching material. Calibration is checked at intervals and again at the end. The A-scan display is watched for a doubled echo or lamination, and high-temperature couplant with temperature compensation is used on hot lines. Readings are written down with location and later entered in a grid or table.

For welds, angle-beam probes of 45, 60 or 70 degrees are selected by thickness and joint design. A distance-amplitude curve or reference level is built on side-drilled holes, the weld and the heat-affected zone are scanned from the accessible sides, and each reflector is sized by length and amplitude before it is compared with the acceptance table. Where access is limited, as it often is on dock piping and tight pipe racks, the report states the coverage achieved and what could not be reached.

Surface preparation and couplant on refinery steel

Ultrasound enters steel only through a continuous couplant film. Heavy scale and flaking paint, common on coastal equipment, must be removed from each point, and a small ground flat is sometimes needed on pitted metal. Couplant choice follows temperature: gel works for ambient lines, while heated lines need a high-temperature product. The report records spot preparation so the next survey can use the same points.

Turning Beaumont readings into corrosion rates

A survey becomes useful when it can be compared with an earlier one. If a Beaumont unit already has baseline thickness data, technicians return to the same marked points, and the change in wall between two dates, divided by the time elapsed, gives a short-term corrosion rate. Dividing the margin above minimum required wall by that rate gives the owner a first estimate of remaining life, which the authorized inspector then confirms. In the Golden Triangle, where crude slates and processing severity change over the years, long-term and short-term rates can differ sharply, and a report that shows both helps the corrosion engineer decide which to trust. Consistent probes, calibration method and grid spacing keep measurement scatter from masquerading as metal loss. When a reading rises between surveys, the report flags it as a probable positioning or surface issue instead of averaging it away.

Weld examination at tank, dock and shop work

Weld UT around Beaumont is less about new refinery units and more about the steady flow of repairs: nozzle replacements on vessels, patch plates on tank shells, new supports on dock piping and shop-built spools. Shear-wave examination is agreed in advance with the owner as the volumetric method, and the procedure states beam angles, scan coverage and the acceptance table. On a tank shell repair, access is often one-sided and the weld cap may be left unground, which limits coverage, so the report lists the surfaces scanned and the zones that could not be reached. In a fabrication yard the same procedure is easier to apply, since parts can be positioned and the weld examined before painting.

Who does the work

Level II technicians perform and interpret the examination under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Procedure approval and report review sit with the founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, whose ASNT NDT Level III credentials cover UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis has no office, laboratory or equipment depot in Beaumont; technicians travel to your site with calibrated instruments and reference blocks, and travel and site-entry requirements are agreed during planning.

What a Beaumont UT report contains

  • Equipment identification, drawing reference and the grid or location identifiers used.
  • Procedure and revision, governing code and edition, and the acceptance table applied.
  • Instrument, probe and block details, and the calibration checks recorded during the job.
  • Technician name and level with the Level III reviewer.
  • For thickness work, readings against nominal and minimum wall, with locations that could not be read noted.
  • For weld work, each reflector's position, length and amplitude, its accept or reject disposition, and coverage limits.

Readings below the owner's alert threshold are called out at the top of the report so they reach the right person quickly.

Tank bottoms and shell courses

Aboveground storage tanks along the Neches and Sabine make up a large part of Beaumont thickness work. Shell courses are read in vertical lines from the foundation to the top, the annular plate and critical zone near the shell-to-bottom junction are read more densely, and nozzle necks and manway necks get their own points. Floor plate readings from the outside only reach so far, since coating, sediment and plate lap limit what a probe sees, so many owners treat the thickness data as a screening input to the API 653 evaluation instead of a final answer. The report states the grid used on each course so the owner can see exactly what was covered.

Planning a UT job in Beaumont

Gulf Coast weather and plant logistics set the pace. Summer heat and humidity heat-soak uninsulated steel and wear down technicians on scaffolds, and hurricane season can shut gates and close the ports for days. Many plants in the Golden Triangle require contractor orientation, TWIC credentials at marine terminals and permits for each area, and turnaround weeks bring large numbers of contractors onto the same units. Lodging near Beaumont tightens during major outages, so technician travel should be booked early. Insulation windows and scaffold access should be arranged by the owner before the technicians arrive, since waiting for a scaffold costs the same as working. Weld examination at fabrication yards is easier to schedule because the work is accessible and the weather matters less.

UT, MT or PT for your Beaumont job

Choose UT for remaining wall or buried weld flaws. For a surface crack at a carbon steel toe or nozzle weld, magnetic particle inspection in Beaumont is typically faster, and for stainless or alloy surfaces dye penetrant inspection in Beaumont is the surface method. Many repair packages pair a surface method with UT. The national ultrasonic testing page explains the method, the Article 5 and 23 thickness measurement guide covers the rules, and the Texas inspection services hub lists related work.

Training your own UT technicians

Plants and contractors in the Golden Triangle often prefer to qualify their own technicians. UT Level 1 training and UT Level 2 training use online theory, simulator practice and practical sessions at the employer's facility, with qualification governed by the employer's written practice. See NDT training in Beaumont and the eligibility checker.

faq.q: Which Beaumont facilities typically need ultrasonic thickness surveys?
faq.a: Refineries, petrochemical units, tank farms, marine dock piping and chemical plants in the Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange area use thickness surveys to track corrosion on piping, vessels and storage tanks.

faq.q: Do I need TWIC to work at Beaumont marine terminals?
faq.a: Access to secure marine terminals normally requires a Transportation Worker Identification Credential or an escort, plus the terminal safety orientation. Confirm the requirement with the terminal operator while planning the job.

faq.q: Can UT measure thickness through coating?
faq.a: Sometimes, if the procedure has been demonstrated through that coating, but thick or disbonded coating gives false readings. Most owners ask for the coating to be removed at each reading point.

faq.q: How are thickness locations kept consistent between surveys?
faq.a: Locations are marked on isometrics or vessel sketches and sometimes on the metal itself, and the same grid spacing and probe type are used each time so differences reflect corrosion and not measurement scatter.

faq.q: Who decides if a pipe can stay in service after a UT survey?
faq.a: The owner and its authorized inspector decide, using API 570 or the applicable code. Atlantis delivers the readings and flags locations below the thresholds the owner has set.

faq.q: Can UT replace radiography on welds?
faq.a: Only where the code, the owner, the engineer and the authorized inspector agree. ASME B31.3 and API 1104 have provisions for ultrasonic examination, and AWS D1.1 has its own groove-weld criteria.

faq.q: What if surfaces are too rough for a reading?
faq.a: The technician reports the location as not read, and the owner can arrange grinding or cleaning so a second visit or a later pass can capture it. Rough surfaces should never be reported as sound.

faq.q: Does UT work on cast or stainless welds?
faq.a: It can, but coarse grain scatters and attenuates the sound, so the procedure must be shown to work on a representative block before it is approved for the weld.

faq.q: Can readings be taken on lines that are operating?
faq.a: Often yes, within the procedure temperature limits and the plant safety rules. Hot service needs a high-temperature probe and couplant, and the plant must approve work on the running line before technicians start.

faq.q: How are thin-wall or heavily pitted surfaces handled?
faq.a: The technician uses a dual-element probe, watches the A-scan for a doubled or distorted echo, and may grind a small flat spot. Locations that still cannot be read are reported as not read.

faq.q: What do you need to quote a Beaumont thickness survey?
faq.a: Send the equipment list, line numbers or tags, materials, nominal wall, operating temperature, insulation status, number of locations, outage dates and any earlier survey data.

faq.q: Can my staff learn ultrasonic testing through Atlantis?
faq.a: Yes. UT Level 1 and Level 2 training combine online theory, simulator practice and practical work at your facility, and a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A governs qualification at your company.

mt.title: Mag Particle Testing (MT) in Beaumont, TX | MPI
mt.description: Magnetic particle inspection for Beaumont refinery welds, dock steel, tank attachments and fabricated vessels. Yoke MT on site. Request a quote today.
mt.h1: Magnetic Particle Testing (MT) in Beaumont, Texas
mt.html:
Magnetic particle testing locates surface and near-surface cracks in ferromagnetic steel, and the Golden Triangle is built largely of it. Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to Beaumont refineries, chemical plants, marine terminals and fabrication yards to examine welds, attachments, nozzles and forgings, with procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III. Tell us about the parts, the code and the schedule in a Beaumont MT quote request.

Where MT fits the Beaumont industrial base

The Beaumont and Port Arthur refineries together process well over a million barrels a day, and the chemical plants around them add heat exchangers, reactors and long pipe racks. Each shell has nozzle welds, each rack has support attachments, and each repair leaves new weld metal that an owner may want examined for surface cracking. Storage tanks in the tank farms along the Neches and Sabine have shell-to-bottom welds, nozzle reinforcement pads, roof structure and clip attachments, all in carbon steel.

The ports bring a second population of steel: dock structures, mooring hardware, loading-arm supports, cranes and the rigging used to lift pipe and modules. Fabrication yards in the area build skids and vessels, and welders there produce structural and pressure welds that are examined at hold points. Even a small marine repair yard produces lifting lugs and pad eyes that demand periodic surface checks. Salt air and humidity corrode exposed steel faster than inland air, so coating breakdown and pitting add surface cracks to the list of things to find.

What MT can and cannot see

MT sets up a magnetic field in the part. A crack or seam that interrupts the field leaks flux, and fine iron particles collect over the leakage as a visible line. Because it depends on magnetism, the method works on carbon steel, low-alloy steel and martensitic grades and not on austenitic stainless, aluminum or copper alloys. Sensitivity is highest at the surface and fades quickly with depth, so MT misses buried lack of fusion that ultrasonic examination would find.

Field direction matters. Flux leaks most strongly when it crosses the flaw at about ninety degrees, which is why every area is examined with two field directions. Coatings, rust, weld spatter and oil reduce sensitivity and can hold false particle buildups. Sharp geometry changes, such as the edge of a nozzle pad, can produce nonrelevant indications that the examiner must recognize and set aside, and a technician with refinery experience knows which ones to expect.

Codes and acceptance for Beaumont MT work

The method is written down in ASME Section V Article 7. ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 6 gives MT methods and acceptance standards for pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.3 and Table 341.3.2 address process piping, and AWS D1.1 covers structural weldments, with AWS D1.5 for bridge steel. ASTM E709 and E1444 describe the guide and practice. Tank repair programs reference API 653, and the owner's inspector establishes the examination scope within it.

Texas regulates boilers under Chapter 755 of the Health and Safety Code through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, and owners of covered process units manage mechanical integrity under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(j). The owner's authorized inspector decides acceptance and repair priority; Atlantis performs the MT examination and reports every indication against the named criteria. Pipeline welding follows API 1104, which includes magnetic particle provisions.

Technique: yokes, particles and demagnetization

Field work usually uses an electromagnetic yoke. The procedure requires an AC yoke to lift at least 10 pounds at the maximum pole spacing used, and a DC or permanent-magnet yoke to lift at least 40 pounds, and the technician proves it with a test weight. The yoke is placed across the weld twice, roughly at right angles, so cracks in any direction are caught. Prods may be allowed on some forgings and castings but are often banned on finished pressure surfaces because of arc strikes.

Visible dry powder works on warm and rough surfaces outdoors, visible wet particles in aerosols suit cleaner welds under a thin layer of white contrast paint, and fluorescent particles under UV-A light give the highest sensitivity in a darkened enclosure. When residual magnetism would affect welding, machining or instruments, the part is demagnetized afterward. The technician records the yoke checks, particle type and light levels.

Surface preparation on coastal steel

Salt-laden air leaves a layer of rust and old coating on many Beaumont structures, and particles stick to it. Welds are normally ground or brushed back to bright metal over the examination area plus a margin of base metal on each side. Where coating cannot be removed, the Level III may approve a procedure demonstrated through thin tight coating, but the owner should expect reduced sensitivity. Technicians list any area that could not be prepared in the report.

Castings, forgings and shop-built parts

Machine shops and fabricators around Beaumont also use MT outside the plant fence. Forgings for flanges, couplings and pressure fittings, castings for valve bodies and pump housings, and heavy weldments for skids all pass through examination at the shop stage. Here the technician often has a bench unit or a coil to magnetize the part, and field direction is controlled by how the part sits in the coil or between contacts. A field indicator or gauss reading confirms the field is adequate before particles go on. The advantage of shop MT is control: parts can be cleaned in a wash tank, examined under proper ultraviolet light in a dark booth and demagnetized on the same bench, which gives the most repeatable result the method can deliver.

Who performs and reviews the work

MT technicians are qualified as Level II under the company written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Procedures and report review come from the founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, who holds ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis has no office, depot or laboratory in Beaumont, so technicians travel to your site with their own yokes, particles, light meters and test weights, mobilized for the agreed scope.

What a Beaumont MT report records

  • Weld, part or tag identification with a sketch of the area examined.
  • Procedure number, revision level, governing code edition and the acceptance table applied.
  • Equipment, yoke lift test results, particle type, contrast paint and light readings.
  • Surface temperature and condition.
  • Each indication by location, length and orientation, with relevant or nonrelevant and accept or reject.
  • Technician name and level, Level III reviewer and date.

Rejected cracks are marked for the repair crew and re-examined after grinding, with the result added to the same record.

Tank farm and dock steel

Storage tanks are a large share of Beaumont MT demand. Shell-to-bottom welds, nozzle reinforcement pad welds, roof-support clips and ladder or stair attachments are all places where fatigue and corrosion fatigue cracks can start, and repair programs reference API 653 for what must be examined after a repair. Inside a tank, MT on the bottom-to-shell fillet is usually done after the surface is blasted or wire-brushed, which makes it a natural step in a tank turnaround. Dock and marine structures add rigging points, mooring hardware and crane foundations, where cyclic loading and saltwater exposure shorten fatigue life. The owner's maintenance program or the manufacturer's rating supplies acceptance criteria for these items, and the Level III writes the procedure around them.

Common indications and how they are judged

A crack usually appears as a sharp, tight line of particles along the weld toe or in the heat-affected zone, while lack of fusion at the surface shows as a straighter line along the fusion boundary. Surface porosity and slag show as rounded or irregular groups. Not every particle cluster is a flaw: an abrupt section change, the edge of a weld cap and magnetic writing from other steel can all hold particles. The examiner re-cleans, remagnetizes and changes field direction to separate relevant from nonrelevant indications, and only relevant ones are measured against the acceptance table. A rejected crack is marked, ground out and re-examined before welding resumes.

Planning an MT job in Beaumont

Weather is the main constraint. Midsummer steel can be hot enough to damage contrast paint or dry particle carriers before the examination is finished, while thunderstorms and heavy humidity wash particles off outdoor welds, so work moves to mornings and shade. Fluorescent examination needs a darkened tent or a night window, which must be approved by the plant. Marine terminals can require TWIC credentials and escorts, and refineries require orientation and area permits. During a large outage the area is crowded, so confirm that surface preparation and scaffolds are ready before the crew travels. Hurricane season should be built into the schedule for any exposed work in late summer.

Scoping an MT job so the visit is productive

A short pre-job exchange saves most of the delays on an MT visit. Tell us the material grade, because some stainless and duplex grades are weakly magnetic or not at all. Send a list of weld numbers or a marked-up drawing, say whether welds are as-welded or ground flush, and note whether insulation, fireproofing or scaffolding will be in the way. State whether the owner bans prods or contrast paint on the equipment, and which acceptance table applies. If fluorescent examination is wanted, ask the plant early about a dark enclosure or a night window. With that information the technician arrives with the right yoke, particles and lights, and the work proceeds weld by weld without improvisation.

MT, PT or UT for your Beaumont job

For carbon steel and surface cracking, MT is usually the efficient choice. For stainless steel or alloy, use liquid penetrant testing in Beaumont. For remaining wall or buried flaws, use ultrasonic testing in Beaumont. The national magnetic particle testing page, the MT complete guide and the Texas inspection hub give more background.

Training your own MT technicians

Employers who run steady weld repair programs often train inspectors in-house. MT Level 1 training and MT Level 2 training combine online theory with practical sessions at your facility under your written practice. See NDT training in Beaumont for all methods.

faq.q: Does salt air affect magnetic particle inspection in Beaumont?
faq.a: Indirectly. Salt air speeds rust and coating breakdown, which reduces particle mobility, so welds need to be ground or brushed to clean metal before examination and any unprepared area noted in the report.

faq.q: Can MT be used on stainless steel tanks?
faq.a: Austenitic stainless is not ferromagnetic, so MT does not work on it. Liquid penetrant is the usual surface method for stainless shells, nozzles and attachments.

faq.q: What is the difference between dry powder and wet particle MT?
faq.a: Dry powder is practical on hot or rough surfaces outdoors. Wet particles, visible or fluorescent, give finer sensitivity on clean welds, and fluorescent systems need UV-A light in a darkened area.

faq.q: Can you examine crane hooks and dock lifting gear?
faq.a: Yes. Surface cracks at load-bearing corners are a standard MT target, and the owner or manufacturer specification supplies the acceptance criteria that the procedure names.

faq.q: Is MT enough to accept a pressure vessel repair?
faq.a: It depends on the repair code and the owner program. MT shows surface cracking, so a repair may also require UT or another volumetric method, with the authorized inspector deciding acceptance.

faq.q: What happens to a cracked weld after MT finds it?
faq.a: The indication is marked and reported. The repair crew removes it by grinding and re-welds, and the area is re-examined with MT to confirm the crack is gone before the repair is accepted.

faq.q: Does coating have to be removed for MT?
faq.a: Thin tight coating may be acceptable if the procedure was demonstrated through it, but thick or flaking coating reduces sensitivity. Most specifications call for bare metal over the weld.

faq.q: Is demagnetization always required?
faq.a: No. It is needed when residual magnetism would affect later welding, machining or instrument operation. The procedure sets the requirement and the report records the result.

faq.q: How do you check that the yoke is strong enough?
faq.a: The technician performs a lift test with a standard weight: at least 10 pounds for an AC yoke and 40 pounds for a DC or permanent-magnet yoke at the pole spacing used, and records the result.

faq.q: Can MT be applied to tank shell welds after a repair?
faq.a: Yes. Shell-to-bottom welds, nozzle pad welds and attachments on carbon steel tanks are typical targets, and the owner program following API 653 sets which welds require examination.

faq.q: Is any special lighting needed for MT?
faq.a: Visible particles need adequate white light at the surface, and fluorescent particles need UV-A light with limited ambient white light. The procedure sets the intensity, and the technician measures it with a meter.

faq.q: How do I request an MT quote for Beaumont?
faq.a: Send the equipment type, material, number of welds or parts, surface condition, applicable code and the schedule or outage that sets the timing, and we will scope the work around site access rules.

pt.title: Liquid Penetrant Testing & Dye Penetrant | Beaumont, TX
pt.description: Dye penetrant inspection for Beaumont and Port Arthur stainless piping, heat exchangers, overlays and marine components. Technicians travel to site. Quote.
pt.h1: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) in Beaumont, Texas
pt.html:
Liquid penetrant testing shows cracks and other flaws that are open to the surface of any non-porous material. Atlantis NDT mobilizes Level II technicians to Beaumont-area refineries, chemical plants, marine terminals and fabrication yards to examine stainless and alloy welds, heat exchanger components, castings and machined parts, with procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III. Describe your materials and code in a Beaumont PT quote request.

Where PT fits the Beaumont and Port Arthur economy

Chemicals and plastics are about three and a half times as concentrated in the Beaumont-Port Arthur area as in the US as a whole, and ethane crackers, including a large TotalEnergies and Borealis unit that began operating in Port Arthur in 2022, process corrosive streams in alloy and stainless equipment. Those plants contain duplex and austenitic piping, nickel alloy lines, exchanger tubesheets and weld overlay, none of which respond to magnetic methods. Penetrant is how surface cracking is found on them during turnarounds and after repair welds.

Refineries and marine terminals add to the mix. Valve and pump repair shops in Beaumont examine machined and cast parts before reassembly. Marine yards on the Neches and Sabine work on aluminum and stainless deck hardware, heat exchange packages and piping that see saltwater. Even carbon steel welds get penetrant when a coated or irregular area makes a magnetic yoke awkward. In a metro area with a large industrial workforce, the common thread is non-magnetic material and critical surface condition.

What PT can and cannot find

The liquid seeps into a surface-breaking crack, lap, seam or pore, excess is removed, and a developer draws the liquid back out so the flaw appears as a colored or fluorescent line. Anything not open to the surface stays invisible: buried lack of fusion, inclusions and subsurface laminations are beyond its reach. A crack smeared shut by grinding, peening or abrasive cleaning may not accept penetrant at all, and oil, paint or process residue can block entry.

Porous surfaces soak up penetrant and glow with background that hides small flaws. Extremely rough weld profiles give a high background and false readings that a trained examiner must separate from cracking. PT does not tell how deep a crack goes, and it does not measure wall loss. Where depth or thickness is the question, UT is the better tool.

Codes and acceptance criteria for Beaumont PT work

ASME Section V Article 6 sets the penetrant method. ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 8 covers PT for pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.4 with Table 341.3.2 covers process piping, and ASTM E165 is the general practice. Stainless fabrication may follow AWS D1.6, while repair of boilers and pressure vessels follows the National Board Inspection Code, with the Texas Boiler Act in Chapter 755 of the Health and Safety Code applying to boilers in the state.

The owner's in-service inspection program, whether API 510 for vessels or API 570 for piping, sets how often surface examination is called for, and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(j) makes inspection part of mechanical integrity. The authorized inspector accepts the results. Atlantis performs the examination and records each indication against the named acceptance table.

Technique, step by step

The area is cleaned by mechanical means and solvent, then dried. The standard temperature range for the part and the penetrant materials is 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit, and outside it the procedure must be qualified for the temperature. Penetrant is applied by spray or brush and held for the dwell time stated in the procedure, then removed by solvent wipe, water wash or post-emulsification, depending on the system. A thin film of developer is applied and given development time before the technician examines the surface under white light or UV-A light in a darkened area.

The technician measures and evaluates each indication against the acceptance criteria, marks rejects, and records the system, batch numbers, dwell, development time and temperature. Post-cleaning follows when the part will be welded, coated or placed in a chemical service where residues could cause trouble.

Materials control for stainless and nickel alloys

Penetrant materials for austenitic stainless, nickel alloys and titanium must be low in halogens and sulfur because residues can cause cracking at elevated temperature. Owners in the Golden Triangle's chemical plants often request batch certificates for each product lot, and the procedure lists the approved brands and the removal steps. The same materials control matters when equipment is going back into service in hot caustic or high-temperature duty, so the technician keeps cans separated by alloy group and records the batch used.

High-sensitivity systems for critical service

Some equipment in the Golden Triangle runs in services where a very small crack matters: hydrogen-bearing units, rotating machinery and highly stressed forgings. Owners often specify a fluorescent system at a higher sensitivity level for those items, with a longer dwell and a controlled development time. The trade-off is that background fluorescence from rough or poorly washed surfaces rises with sensitivity, so cleaning care increases and the area must be darkened. The batch and sensitivity level are written in the report so a later reviewer can see exactly what system was used on which part.

Who does the work

PT is performed by Level II technicians qualified under the company's SNT-TC-1A-based written practice. Level III oversight rests with Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, who signs off procedures and reads each report. Atlantis has no office, laboratory or depot in Beaumont, so technicians travel to your facility carrying the cleaners, penetrant, developer, lights and comparator blocks they need.

What the PT report includes

  • Part or weld identification, material and area examined.
  • Procedure and revision, code and acceptance table, penetrant system and sensitivity level.
  • Manufacturer and batch numbers, with contaminant certificate reference where needed.
  • Surface temperature, dwell time and development time.
  • Each indication by location, size and type, with relevant or nonrelevant and the accept or reject call.
  • Technician and Level III reviewer names, dates and photographs where helpful.

Rejected areas are marked, repaired and re-examined, and the result stays in the same record.

Common indications and how they are judged

Cracks show as continuous or broken colored or fluorescent lines, porosity as rounded dots, and laps or cold shuts as irregular lines on the surface. How quickly a bleedout spreads tells the examiner something: a fast, broad stain suggests a wide opening, while a slow faint line suggests a tight crack. Nonrelevant indications arise from rough weld ripples, residual penetrant in a thread or a poorly removed excess, and the technician re-cleans and re-tests the area to confirm. Relevant indications are measured and compared with the acceptance table, with linear indications judged by length and rounded ones by size and spacing. The outcome is written as accepted or rejected, and rejected flaws are marked, repaired and re-examined.

Precleaning and surface condition

Most poor penetrant results begin with poor cleaning. Equipment from process service carries hydrocarbon films, amine, caustic and polymer residues that fill cracks and keep penetrant out, and abrasive blasting or wire brushing can smear metal over fine openings. A sound sequence is mechanical removal of scale and coating, solvent or detergent cleaning, and a drying period long enough for solvent to leave the flaw. On overlay and cladding, a light etch can reopen smeared surfaces when the procedure allows it. Cleaners must also suit the alloy, since chloride-bearing products are not acceptable on austenitic stainless. The technician records the cleaning method so a later reviewer can see how the surface was prepared.

Shop and field setups

A penetrant line in a shop, with controlled light and measured dwell, gives the most repeatable results, but most Beaumont plant work is done in the field with aerosol cans and wipe-off cleaning. Wind, dust and sun affect dwell and developer thickness in the field, so experienced examiners work in shade, apply developer in thin even coats and time each step. When a specification requires water-washable penetrant on rough castings, the shop line is the better choice, and the procedure states which setup applies so shop and field results remain comparable.

Planning a PT job in Beaumont

Summer afternoons push exposed steel past the upper temperature limit, so work is usually done early or in shade. Cold snaps, though less common than on the Great Lakes, can bring parts under the lower limit by dawn. Humidity slows drying and rain stops outdoor work. Penetrant materials are flammable and chemical, so plants may restrict aerosols near operating units and require safety data sheets and permits. Marine terminals can require TWIC credentials. Preparation by the owner or fabricator, with weld spatter ground off and process residue removed, saves a trip. During hurricane season, plan buffers for late summer work.

Scoping a PT job so the visit is productive

Good information up front keeps a penetrant visit short. List the alloys, because stainless, nickel alloy and titanium call for controlled materials and carbon steel does not. Send weld numbers or a marked drawing, and say whether the surfaces are as-welded, ground or blasted. Note the expected temperature on the day, whether the equipment will be open or closed, and whether solvents or aerosols are restricted at the site. If fluorescent examination is required, ask the plant about a darkened area. State the acceptance table that governs, and whether the owner wants batch records for each product lot. With that information the technician can bring the right system and complete the examination weld by weld.

PT, MT or UT for your Beaumont job

Use PT for non-magnetic metal or awkward geometry. For carbon steel where speed and sensitivity matter, magnetic particle inspection in Beaumont may be quicker, and for wall loss or buried flaws ultrasonic testing in Beaumont is the method. The general penetrant testing page, the Article 6 explainer and the MT versus PT comparison give more detail.

Training your own PT technicians

Penetrant is often the first method a new inspector learns. PT Level 1 training and PT Level 2 training combine online theory, practice on the penetrant testing simulator and hands-on sessions at your facility. See NDT training in Beaumont for other methods.

faq.q: Why is penetrant testing common on Beaumont chemical plant equipment?
faq.a: Plants in the Golden Triangle use plenty of stainless, duplex and nickel alloy, which are not magnetic, so liquid penetrant is the practical surface method for finding cracks on welds, overlays and machined parts.

faq.q: What penetrant temperature range applies?
faq.a: The standard range for the part and the penetrant materials is 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Outside it, the procedure must be qualified for the temperature, which can matter in summer sun or after a cold night.

faq.q: Can PT find a crack under paint?
faq.a: No. The flaw must be open to the surface, so paint and coating must be removed first. Coating that bridges a crack will block penetrant entry and hide the indication.

faq.q: Are special penetrants needed on stainless steel?
faq.a: Yes. Products with controlled halogen and sulfur content are used on austenitic stainless and nickel alloys, with batch records kept, and the surface is cleaned afterward as the procedure states.

faq.q: How long does the penetrant need to sit?
faq.a: The dwell time is set by the procedure for the material, flaw type and temperature, and is typically several minutes. The technician times it and records it in the report.

faq.q: Does PT work on aluminum marine components?
faq.a: Yes. Aluminum is non-magnetic and non-porous, so penetrant works well for cracks and porosity on marine components, with care taken over cleaning and over smeared metal left by grinding.

faq.q: Is fluorescent PT more sensitive than visible?
faq.a: Generally yes, and it is favored for critical or fatigue-prone parts, but it needs UV-A light and a darkened area. Visible penetrant is simpler in daylight at many field welds.

faq.q: Can PT be used on hot welds?
faq.a: Only within the procedure temperature limits. Hot welds can evaporate penetrant before it dwells, so the weld is cooled into range or a procedure qualified for higher temperature is used.

faq.q: What cleanup follows a penetrant examination?
faq.a: Residual penetrant and developer are removed after evaluation, especially on parts to be welded, coated or placed in chemical or oxygen service. The procedure states the method and the report records it.

faq.q: Who evaluates a penetrant indication?
faq.a: The Level II technician evaluates it against the named acceptance table, and a Level III reviews the report. The owner and its authorized inspector decide on repair or further evaluation where the code requires.

faq.q: What do you need for a PT quote in Beaumont?
faq.a: Send the materials, component types, number of welds or parts, surface condition, code, chemical restrictions and the outage or schedule that sets the timing, and we will scope the work around site rules.

rt.description: Atlantis does not perform radiography in the US. For Beaumont welds we offer ultrasonic examination where code allows and Level III review of images.
rt.h1: Radiographic Testing in Beaumont, Texas: What Atlantis Does and Does Not Offer
rt.html:
Radiographic testing is not something Atlantis NDT does, and Atlantis does not perform radiography anywhere in the United States. Industrial radiography depends on radioactive sources or X-ray equipment and is licensed by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 CFR Part 34 or by an Agreement State such as Texas under equivalent rules. It is not a service we sell in Beaumont, Port Arthur or anywhere else in the country. If you were looking for radiography for a Golden Triangle project, here is what we can do.

Ultrasonic examination of welds in the Beaumont area

On many process piping and vessel welds around Beaumont, shear-wave ultrasonic examination looks through the full thickness of the weld for lack of fusion, cracks and slag. Technicians are mobilized to your plant, terminal or fabrication yard for the agreed scope. Whether that examination may stand in for radiography depends on the governing document. ASME B31.3 and API 1104 both include ultrasonic options for production welds, AWS D1.1 sets separate acceptance criteria for groove welds, and ASME Section VIII allows ultrasonic examination in place of radiography only under specific conditions. The owner, the engineer and, for code work, the authorized inspector must agree before work begins. See ultrasonic testing in Beaumont, or send details through the Beaumont quote request.

Level III review of images and procedures, with no radiation licence needed

Looking at an image exposes no one to radiation, so an ASNT Level III can review work another party has produced. The founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, holds ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and can check film or digital images and technique sheets against ASME Section V Article 2 and the construction code. Beaumont owners and contractors typically ask for:

  • A second read of disputed or borderline indications before a weld is cut out.
  • A check of image quality, sensitivity indicator, density and coverage on a finished package.
  • Review of a radiography contractor's written procedure and technique sheets.
  • Review of the contractor's written practice and qualification records.

We review submitted records only, never source handling or exposures. We do not recommend or name radiography contractors, and exposure planning remains with the licensed provider and your site safety staff.

If the project specification calls for film or images, the licensed provider you choose will normally issue them with a technique sheet, and the review described above can be arranged under a separate agreement from that contract. Owners often ask for the review before a repair crew cuts out a weld, because a second read can prevent unnecessary rework.

Surface methods that go with a volumetric examination

Repair packages around Beaumont often combine volumetric and surface examination. Magnetic particle testing in Beaumont covers carbon and low-alloy steel, and liquid penetrant testing in Beaumont covers stainless steel, nickel alloys and aluminum. The Texas inspection services hub lists the conventional examinations we offer.

Because the review is a paper and image exercise, it can be arranged for a project anywhere in the Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange area without any site mobilization at all, which keeps the cost of a second opinion small relative to the cost of cutting out a sound weld.

Radiography theory training and written practice support

Studying radiography theory needs no licence, though handling sources does. Our RT Level 2 course covers principles, interpretation and code criteria, and source handling belongs to the licensed employer. Companies that qualify their own staff can use Level III consulting and written practice development to build a program around ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The Beaumont NDT training page lists the rest, and the quote form above reaches the same team for any of these requests.

faq.q: Is radiography available from Atlantis in Beaumont?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not perform radiographic testing in the United States, because industrial radiography requires a radioactive materials or X-ray licence. Ultrasonic examination and Level III review of radiographs are the services we provide instead.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic testing replace radiography on Beaumont pipe welds?
faq.a: Sometimes. ASME B31.3 and API 1104 have provisions for ultrasonic examination, and AWS D1.1 has groove-weld criteria. The owner, engineer and authorized inspector must agree before work starts.

faq.q: Can you review images produced by another contractor?
faq.a: Yes. A Level III can review film or digital images and technique sheets against ASME Section V Article 2 and the construction code, giving a documented second opinion without any radiation work.

faq.q: Do you name or recommend a radiography contractor?
faq.a: No. Select a licensed provider through your own approved vendor process and site safety rules. We can review the procedure and the results afterward if you ask, and document our findings.

faq.q: Can my staff learn radiographic theory with Atlantis?
faq.a: Yes. The RT Level 2 course covers theory and interpretation. Source handling and exposure work require a licence held by the employer, so those parts fall outside our scope.
